name: US Tribal Class III (NIGC / Tribal-State Compact) Market Profile

regulator.name: National Indian Gaming Commission (NIGC), alongside tribes and states
regulator.notes: NIGC regulates alongside tribes and states, covering more than 500 gaming establishments operated by nearly 250 tribes across 29 states. Day-to-day device regulation for Class III is by the Tribal Gaming Regulatory Agency (TGRA).

bindingStandards.name: 25 CFR Part 543 (Minimum Internal Control Standards) - CLASS II
25 CFR Part 547 (Minimum Technical Standards for Class II Gaming Systems and Equipment) - CLASS II
Tribal-State compact or Secretarial procedures - CLASS III
bindingStandards.notes: THERE IS NO NIGC TECHNICAL STANDARD FOR CLASS III. Class III device standards derive from the compact and are enforced by the TGRA. Each compact must be reviewed individually.

minimum.value: No federal minimum; set by compact
minimum.notes: Compact examples: Arizona Tribal-State Compact 80% to 83% for Class III over expected machine life (MEDIUM); Wisconsin compacts require electronic games of chance to pay out between 80% and 100% over the device life cycle (MEDIUM). DO NOT infer tribal requirements from state commercial standards.

minimumAge.notes: Compact and tribal law dependent; commonly 18 or 21.

retentionPeriod.notes: 25 CFR 543/547 for Class II; Class III per compact.

certification.labModel: 25 CFR 547 requires submission to a testing laboratory (Class II)
certification.notes: Per NIGC's Technical Standards Q&A Bulletin, a gaming system need only be submitted to a testing laboratory once. https://www.nigc.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Tech-Stds-QA-Bulletin.pdf

verificationRequired: The current legal status of 25 CFR Part 542 MICS as applied to Class III following the Colorado River Indian Tribes litigation - MUST be confirmed by counsel, as it determines whether NIGC MICS bind Class III operations
The specific Tribal-State compact for each target tribe: RTP, stake caps, age, RG requirements, retention
TGRA-specific technical requirements and approval process
consultantNotes: This is not a single market. It is a per-compact, per-TGRA patchwork. Any engagement must be scoped to specific tribes, and the compact obtained.
The Class II / Class III distinction is decisive: Class II has federal technical standards (25 CFR 547), Class III does not. Confirm which class the product targets before anything else.
